title: Make, do, take, have
what: translated verb-noun collocations ('make a photo', 'do a mistake', 'make sport', 'take a decision' in American English, 'make a party')
summary: This error persists due to direct translation from native languages and early learning habits. It subtly undermines fluency and can make communication sound less natural, despite advanced grammatical proficiency.
listenFor: Pay close attention to your verb choices when combining them with common nouns, especially for actions, decisions, and social events.

contrasts.wrong: I always make a photo of the sunset when I am on vacation.
contrasts.right: I always take a photo of the sunset when I am on vacation.
contrasts.note: Take a photo is the standard collocation for capturing an image.

contrasts.wrong: It is important to learn from the mistakes we do.
contrasts.right: It is important to learn from the mistakes we make.
contrasts.note: Make a mistake is the correct idiom for committing an error.

contrasts.wrong: Many people make sport to stay healthy and active.
contrasts.right: Many people do sport to stay healthy and active.
contrasts.note: Do sport or exercise is the correct verb for engaging in physical activity.

contrasts.wrong: We are planning to make a party for her birthday next month.
contrasts.right: We are planning to have a party for her birthday next month.
contrasts.note: Have a party or throw a party is used for hosting a social gathering.

contrasts.wrong: Could you please make me a favor and pick up the dry cleaning?
contrasts.right: Could you please do me a favor and pick up the dry cleaning?
contrasts.note: Do a favor is the correct idiom for performing a helpful act.

probes.sentence: I need to do a phone call to my manager about the new proposal.
answers: I need to make a phone call to my manager about the new proposal.

probes.sentence: She always makes her homework right after school.
answers: She always does her homework right after school.

probes.sentence: We will make a meeting to discuss the budget adjustments.
answers: We will have a meeting to discuss the budget adjustments.

probes.sentence: He did a lot of progress on his dissertation this semester.
answers: He made a lot of progress on his dissertation this semester.
